title: Joint, Marginal & Conditional Distributions
interviewAnswer: A joint distribution describes variables together; marginalization sums/integrates out variables; conditioning updates the distribution given observed information.
why: Joint, Marginal & Conditional Distributions is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: A joint distribution describes variables together; marginalization sums/integrates out variables; conditioning updates the distribution given observed information. Conditional distributions depend on evidence. Bayes rule reverses conditioning. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: From a joint table of device and conversion, derive device marginal rates and P(conversion|device).
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Joint, Marginal & Conditional Distributions have?
How would you validate Joint, Marginal & Conditional Distributions on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
